study.hypothesis: The deterministic symmetric deficit may partly reflect lossy averaging rather than utility of supplied pair rank. Canonicalizing the two complete ten-event blocks by exact content removes supplied orientation while retaining the unordered block inputs before inherited compression. Rank utility predicts a canonical deficit with reversal recovery; canonical recovery beyond symmetric favors an averaging/conditioning explanation. This tests conditional summary dependence: supplied pooling and within-block rank remain, so total sequence invariance is not claimed.

study.proposed_difference: Compare exact offset-major block descriptors: seven int64 fields(item_id,cate_id,campaign_id,customer_id,brand,price_bucket,action), then four binary historical task memberships, for offsets0..9. All three arms perform the same selector/summary work. Measure full cost and compare to the faster original reference; no efficiency improvement is predicted.
falsifiers: Canonical recovery within delta of supplied and materially above symmetric, with a valid reversal control, falsifies necessity of terminal-pair orientation for this summary recipe, not other order effects.
If reversal loses more than delta, a canonical loss cannot isolate orientation utility from compression/conditioning/optimization.
Failed tuple preservation, tie/summary invariance, movement, gradients or supplied bridge parity invalidates attribution; execution failure is distinct from a scientific null.
One seed/small gap without cluster uncertainty is not repeated controlled support. Identical-seed bridges do not count as independent repetition.
alternative_explanations: Canonical routing changes content-position coefficients. Fixed summary compression may favor supplied coordinates; reversal only partly controls this.
The item-ID-first ascending key depends on arbitrary vocab encoding and retained within-block order; it is one replacement, not an optimal invariant encoder.
Authorized task memberships enter tie breaking. When only task masks differ and item tuples match, the summary views must remain identical; verify this.
Averaging removes odd magnitude and can alter optimization/regularization; selection avoids averaging but adds discontinuous content routing.
Pooling, within-block order, pair membership and partial-block location remain supplied. No elapsed-time/real-recency or globally order-free conclusion.
Auxiliary/surrogate training can change all slices. Incumbent improves click while auxiliary AUC is lower than DIN; retain the tradeoff.
